title: Profile and optimize preview generation hotspots
description:
Source: docs/tasks/tickets/CC-008-preview-generation-profiling.md
Source key: CC-008
Source status: In Progress
Source priority: P1

## Summary
Capture actionable preview-generation measurements and identify the highest-value performance work for meshes around 6K triangles.

## Scope
Make detailed editor generation logging toggleable and include the grid dimensions, sampled-corner count, mixed-cell count, SDF gradient-evaluation count, mesh vertex count, triangle count, and per-stage timings. Split MeshExtraction timing into corner classification, contour resolution, vertex welding, and triangle emission, with profiling overhead disabled when detailed diagnostics are off. Indent these timings beneath the aggregate MeshExtraction entry. Use the measurements to benchmark field sampling, mesh extraction, and appearance baking before changing runtime algorithms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detailed preview diagnostics can be enabled or disabled from the editor settings.
- The setting persists across editor-window reloads.
- Disabled diagnostics do not suppress topology warnings or generation errors.
- Enabled diagnostics report grid dimensions, sampled corners, mixed cells, SDF gradient evaluations, mesh counts, and stage timings.
- Enabled diagnostics report MeshActiveCellConstruction, MeshContourResolution, MeshVertexWelding, and MeshTriangleEmission timings beneath the top-level MeshExtraction stage.
- Enabled diagnostics report `TotalGeneration`, calculated from top-level stages only so mesh subtimings are not double-counted.
- Disabled diagnostics avoid per-operation extraction timestamp collection.
- Mesh extraction classification uses a direct contiguous eight-corner grid read instead of repeated coordinate/index calculations.
- Corner classification uses inline range checks for surface epsilon handling in the hot loop; the shared normalization helper remains at endpoint-welding boundaries.
- A benchmark records timings at more than one preview quality and identifies the dominant work.
- Optimization proposals preserve watertightness, welded vertices, deterministic output, and the authoritative DNA boundary.

## Validation
- Static error check reports no errors for the changed editor, runtime, and focused test files after adding extraction counters and cached-grid gradients.
- Cached-grid gradient source path is implemented. Unity probes pass for a centered sphere and overlapping spheres, with zero boundary and non-manifold edges.
- The extractor canonicalizes exact and near-zero surface samples with `ScalarComparisonEpsilon` before contour resolution. The shared tolerance is `1e-3`, which removes the observed tiny contour caps from the authored creature asset.
- Unity probes pass for `first_creature.json`: 2,264 triangles, 1,134 vertices, 0 boundary edges, 0 non-manifold edges, and 3,396 total edges.
- Unity EditMode or manual editor check toggles diagnostics and confirms the expected log behavior.
- Benchmark runs with diagnostics enabled at more than one `VoxelsPerUnit` value. Captured 128x128x128 runs include 2,373 triangles / 1,196 vertices with 743.6 ms extraction, and 2,376 triangles / 1,192 vertices with 740.4 ms extraction.

## Findings
The captured runs make MeshExtraction the dominant stage at 743.6 ms and 740.4 ms, while full-volume FieldSampling is about 175-179 ms for 2,146,689 samples. The latest baseline run produced 1,194 mixed cells and 14,256 SDF gradient evaluations, exactly six probes per emitted triangle (2,376 x 6). A cached-grid finite-difference gradient now removes those SDF probes during extraction. A centered sphere probe at 18x18x18 cells reports 1,208 triangles, 606 vertices, zero boundary edges, and zero non-manifold edges. An overlapping-sphere probe also reports zero boundary and non-manifold edges. The authored creature asset exposed a separate near-zero surface case: a `1e-4` classification tolerance left tiny disconnected caps, while the tested `1e-3` tolerance produced a watertight result. Mixed-cell traversal, contour-resolver allocations, and appearance-bake recompilation remain secondary hypotheses.

The portable Burst sampler reduced `FieldSampling` for the authored `128x128x128` preview from `166.5-184.5 ms` to `45.9-49.2 ms`, but MeshExtraction remained the dominant cost. At `256x256x256`, Burst sampling took `379.7-396.1 ms` while extraction took `944.1-1,048.3 ms`. The output contained 8,858 triangles and 4,431 vertices for the stable samples. A later edited definition produced more mixed cells and up to `1,147.3 ms` extraction, confirming that contour processing, not SDF sampling, controls preview latency at higher quality.

For the current `4x4x4` bounds, `32` voxels/unit produces exactly `128^3 = 16,777,216` cells. `64` voxels/unit would produce `256^3 = 134,217,728` cells and is rejected by the intentional safety budget before allocation. Increasing that ceiling is not a performance fix. It would permit an eightfold larger cell volume while leaving the managed per-cell contour and welding work unchanged.
The first sub-stage report showed only 12.0 ms of contour resolution, 4.0 ms of vertex welding, and 2.0 ms of triangle emission against 907.8 ms of total MeshExtraction. The apparent 976.0 ms corner-classification cost was profiler overhead: a timestamp was collected for every cell, including roughly 2.1 million empty cells. The profiler now timestamps only the mixed-cell boundaries, and the extractor defers corner-position construction until after sign classification, so the next run will measure the real classification/traversal cost. Sub-stage lines are indented beneath the aggregate MeshExtraction entry. Because these timings use per-operation timestamp sampling, the extractor collects them only when detailed diagnostics are enabled; ordinary runtime previews use the unprofiled overload.
The corrected profile measured 484.2 ms extraction, including 463.0 ms classification, before the grid-read optimization. Direct contiguous corner reads reduced the same `first_creature.json` probe to 338.5 ms extraction and 316.0 ms classification. Contour resolution remained 12.0 ms, welding 5.0 ms, and emission 2.0 ms. The optimized result remained watertight with 2,264 triangles, 1,134 vertices, and zero boundary/non-manifold edges.
The subsequent inline epsilon classification reduced the same profiled asset probe to 142.3 ms extraction and 122.0 ms classification. Contour resolution remained 12.0 ms, welding 4.0 ms, and emission 1.0 ms. The result remained watertight with 2,264 triangles, 1,134 vertices, and zero boundary/non-manifold edges.
The diagnostic report now includes a non-double-counted total. `Parallel.For` is not used for SDF sampling yet: the current evaluator is an interface-backed object graph that calls UnityEngine math APIs, and the project has no explicit Burst/Jobs dependency. A future parallel sampling pass should first move the compiled SDF into blittable data and a Burst-compatible evaluator, then compare worker-thread or Job System results against the deterministic scalar baseline.

Slice 1 of the mesh-generation handoff is implemented and validated in the real editor. `ActiveCellBuilder` classifies the dense grid once after sampling and retains only mixed-sign cells (`ActiveCellEntry{CellIndex, CaseIndex}`) in stable increasing global index order. `MarchingCubesExtractor.Extract` now iterates active cells instead of re-classifying the whole volume; the pre-change dense loop is preserved as `ExtractLegacy` (internal reference oracle for parity, visible to tests via `AssemblyInfo.cs`). `MeshExtractionResult` gained `ActiveCellConstructionTime` and `ContourResolutionCallCount`; `GradientEvaluationCount` is now incremented per cached-grid gradient (one per non-degenerate triangle) so the diagnostic is honest.

Parity evidence in the editor (27 runtime tests, executed directly): the active-cell path is byte-for-byte identical to the reference path for the centered sphere (1,208 triangles / 606 vertices, matching the previously recorded reference values), overlapping spheres, empty field, and a v2 BodySpline-with-limb fixture; watertight with zero boundary and non-manifold edges; deterministic across repeated runs; `ContourResolutionCallCount == MixedCellCount` on every fixture (homogeneous cells never reach the resolver). The MCP test runner still discovers zero runtime tests (CC-014 blocker), so tests were invoked through the editor's in-memory compiler.

Current benchmark on the v2 BodySpline-with-limb definition (Body-rooted leg, 2.5 bounds): at `VoxelsPerUnit=16` (80^3, 531,441 samples) total 185.5 ms, FieldSampling 29.6 ms, MeshExtraction 106.8 ms (ActiveCellConstruction 50.0 ms, ContourResolution 41.0 ms, Welding 7.0 ms, Emission 4.0 ms), Validation 3.7 ms, AppearanceBake 45.4 ms; 7,728 mixed cells, 7,674 vertices, 15,336 triangles. At `VoxelsPerUnit=32` (160^3, 4,173,281 samples) total 1,341.2 ms, FieldSampling 253.3 ms, MeshExtraction 867.0 ms (ActiveCellConstruction 442.0 ms, ContourResolution 328.0 ms, Welding 44.0 ms, Emission 28.0 ms), Validation 21.4 ms, AppearanceBake 199.3 ms; 31,056 mixed cells, 29,586 vertices, 59,160 triangles. Active-cell construction and contour resolution dominate; welding is about 5% of extraction, confirming the audit correction that classification/traversal outrank dictionary welding. The dense scan is still the full-volume cost by design; Slice 3 (sparse candidate regions) is what removes empty volume from that scan.

## Preparation Plan (2026-08-23)
No implementation is planned in this review step. The current evidence supports a narrow optimization sequence:

1. Lock a preview-quality budget for the standard 96^3 creature path and keep triangle-count variance within the measured healthy band.
2. Treat `FieldSampling` as the first optimization target because it remains the largest single stage in the debug logs and the existing project notes call out the SDF evaluator as the next major hotspot.
3. Review `AppearanceBake` as the second target because it is consistently the next-largest stage and is already documented as nearest-part + triplanar-noise driven.
4. Keep mesh extraction on the quality guardrail: the current extraction path is already stable, deterministic, and topology-safe; optimization work should not broaden the geometry algorithm unless a benchmark shows a real bottleneck.
5. Use the existing project review files in [Assets/Scripts/README.md](Assets/Scripts/README.md) and [docs/tasks/active-tasks.md](docs/tasks/active-tasks.md) as the source-of-truth constraints while the work is being prepared.

This turns the timings into a disciplined optimization order: target the field sampler first, then appearance, and only then revisit broader generation changes if the quality budget still fails.

## Blockers
The Unity Test Framework job previously stalled at zero progress. Direct Unity probes now cover the centered sphere, overlapping spheres, and `first_creature.json`, but deterministic parity and the post-optimization timed benchmark remain pending.

Latest editor profile supplied on 2026-08-23, using the standard 96x96x96
preview, reported 912,673 samples, 6,754 mixed cells, 13,034 triangles, and
6,519 vertices. FieldSampling took 793.3 ms and AppearanceBake took 325.6 ms.
The log identified Burst sampling as active. This is useful evidence for
CC-045, but it does not prove that all managed SDF consumers have been removed.

## Next Step
Slice 1 is implemented and validated (byte-identical parity, determinism, and a two-quality benchmark recorded above). Proceed to Slice 2 of the handoff: direct integer edge ownership replacing the tuple dictionary in `MarchingCubesExtractor`, then delete the `ExtractLegacy` reference path and its parity tests once the new path is the baseline. Keep `CubeContourResolver`, winding, and active-cell iteration unchanged. Re-run the focused extraction tests and the benchmark after the change.

Findings (code-grounded):
1. FieldSampling = 66-76% of Total, ~linear in sample count. Whole grid sampled incl. empty space; op AABBs exist for culling (CC-062) -> sparse/region-aware sampling is the biggest absolute lever (CC-061).
2. MeshActiveCellConstruction = 66-78% of MeshExtraction and scales with cell volume (149ms@112^3, 398ms@160^3). Root cause: ActiveCellBuilder.Build does a serialized managed full-grid scan (1.4-4.1M cells), 8-corner copy + 8x NormalizeSurfaceDensity per cell, List<ActiveCellEntry> append. Only ~0.5% of cells are mixed.
3. AppearanceBake = 172-304ms. Root cause: PartAppearanceSampler.Resolver.Resolve evaluates EVERY part's compiled SDF program + Body program per vertex (managed evaluator), O(parts x vertices), plus 3x Mathf.PerlinNoise per vertex.
4. Anomaly: 88^3 row is out of line (0.68 us/sample vs 0.53-0.58) - likely mid-edit state; re-capture before using as baseline.

Next step (Slice A started): native-backed DensityGrid + Burst-compiled single-threaded ActiveCellScanJob (deterministic, same ordering), dispose grid in generator + tests. Hypothesis: ActiveCellConstruction 149ms -> <10ms at 112^3 with bit-identical active list.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Slice A (Burst active-cell scan + native grid handoff) — VALIDATED 2026-09-01.

Change: DensityGrid is now native-backed (IDisposable, Persistent NativeArray<float> Samples); the managed float[] copy after sampling is gone. ActiveCellBuilder.Build replaced its serialized managed full-grid scan with a Burst-compiled single-threaded ActiveCellScanJob (IJob, same z/y/x iteration order, identical NormalizeSurfaceDensity semantics; +inf/NaN preserved). CreatureMeshGenerator disposes the grid in a try/finally after extraction. All test call sites wrap grids in using.

Validation:
- dotnet build Runtime + Tests.Runtime: 0 errors.
- Unity compile after refresh: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- PlayMode (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime, full assembly): 417/417 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- get_errors clean on all 11 edited files; git diff --check clean.

Timing evidence (in-editor, dino_creature.json, 112x112x112 cells = 1,442,897 samples, vpu 14.0, 7,408 mixed cells, Burst warmup done):
- Managed-equivalent scan (old path replica): 219.3 ms
- New Burst ActiveCellBuilder.Build: 25.2 ms
- In-environment speedup: 8.7x; vs recorded editor baseline (149.0 ms at 112^3): ~5.9x
- Output bit-identical: managed vs Burst cell index + case index order matches exactly (orderMatches=True).

Residual risk: ActiveCellScanJob is single-threaded by design (deterministic ordering); a later parallel prefix-sum scan could go further but would require a determinism/ordering change. AppearanceBake (O(parts x vertices) managed SDF evals, ~172 ms @112^3) and FieldSampling (region-aware sparse sampling) remain the larger absolute targets.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Slice C (appearance Resolver AABB broad-phase) — VALIDATED 2026-09-01.

Change: PartAppearanceSampler.Resolver now precomputes each part's world AABB + Cullable flag from its compiled SdfProgram root op (data already produced by the CC-062 builder), and Resolve skips a part provably farther than the closest found so far (a Cullable part's SDF is bounded below by distance to its AABB, so skipping is bit-identical). Internal EnableBroadPhase test hook (default true) compares the broad-phase path against the unconditional reference. No pipeline or determinism changes; appearance output is unchanged.

Validation:
- dotnet build clean; Unity compile 0 errors/0 warnings.
- PlayMode ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime 420/420 (was 417; +3 new: far-part-skip, overlapping-AABB nearer-pick, and broad-phase-vs-reference across a point grid incl. active Body field).
- get_errors clean; git diff --check clean.

Timing (in-editor, dino_creature.json at 96^3 = 10,306 tris / 5,155 verts, the exact recorded-baseline fixture):
- AppearanceBaker.Bake 5-run: min 111.9 / median 112.4 / avg 112.7 ms vs recorded baseline 111.9 ms -> NEUTRAL (~0%).

Root cause of neutrality: the dino has 6 parts; per-vertex appearance cost is dominated by the always-evaluated Body program (62 ops) plus the two large limb programs (65 and 107 ops) whose AABBs contain body-surface vertices, so the broad phase skips only the small far parts. The broad phase helps creatures with many spatially-separated parts, not this fixture.

Residual risk / next: the real appearance lever is Burst-ing the per-vertex bake or precomputing the Body field into a coarse grid; FieldSampling (region-aware sparse sampling) remains the biggest absolute target (~507 ms at 96^3).

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Slice B (region-aware FieldSampling root-AABB early exit) — VALIDATED 2026-09-01.

Change: SdfSamplingJob now pre-fills +inf for any corner outside the root op's inflated world AABB (RootHasBounds/RootMinBound/RootMaxBound passed from DensityGrid) and returns before the per-op loop. The containment test mirrors the evaluator's per-op culling test exactly, so outside-root corners (which the evaluator already culls to +inf) are bit-identical; in-bounds corners run the normal path. RootHasBounds=false (standalone-primitive programs) never early-exits.

Rationale measured first: the dino has 252 ops and only 13.3% of grid corners lie inside the root's inflated AABB (86.7% outside), so the dominant per-corner O(ops) AABB scan is skipped for most of the grid.

Validation:
- dotnet build Runtime + Tests.Runtime: 0 errors.
- Unity compile: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- PlayMode (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime): 421/421 passed (+1 new SamplePortable_RegionAwareEarlyExit_MatchesReferenceEvaluator asserting every corner equals SdfProgramEvaluator.Evaluate bit-for-bit and >50% of corners are +inf).
- get_errors clean; git diff --check clean; diff = +85 insertions / 0 deletions (3 files).

Timing (in-editor, dino_creature.json, avg of 3 runs after Burst warmup, new SamplePortable vs recorded editor baselines):
- 96^3: 107.5 ms avg vs 507 ms baseline = ~4.7x faster
- 112^3: 231.3 ms avg (best 185.5) vs 832.8 ms baseline = ~3.6x faster
FieldSampling was 66-76% of TotalGeneration; this removes most of the empty-space cost.

Residual: inside-root corners still pay the full op loop (per-op culling remains); a coarse occupancy grid or op-bucketing could cut further but adds complexity. Next largest target after this: AppearanceBake's always-evaluated Body program (per-vertex bottleneck) or precomputing the Body field into a coarse grid.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Slice D (Burst per-vertex appearance resolution) — VALIDATED 2026-09-01.

Change: new AppearanceResolveBurst (Runtime/Appearance/AppearanceResolveBurst.cs) with two Burst jobs. PartSdfDistanceJob evaluates one compiled SDF program at every vertex (Fast culling, mirrors SdfSamplingJob batching/scratch) writing Abs(distance) into a per-program column (parts 0..N-1, Body column N, +inf pre-filled = absent per CC-064). AppearanceMergeJob picks the nearest finite surface per vertex (strict < for parts, non-strict <= for Body, same as Resolver.Resolve) and outputs baseColor/seed/scale/bodyWins. AppearanceBaker.Bake routes through it by default (internal UseBurstResolve toggle, default true) and keeps the Body vertical gradient (Unity AnimationCurve/Gradient, must render authored data exactly) + triplanar noise (~1%) in a managed tail.

Measured first: of a 107.5 ms bake @96^3 dino, SDF resolution = 104.6 ms (97%), triplanar noise = 1.0 ms (1%).

Validation:
- dotnet build Runtime + Tests.Runtime: 0 errors.
- Unity compile: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- PlayMode (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime): 422/422 (+1 Bake_BurstResolve_MatchesManagedResolveExactly asserting bit-for-bit color equality between Burst and managed paths on a body-with-gradient + protruding-bump-part fixture, exercising both branches).
- get_errors clean; git diff --check clean.

Timing (in-editor, dino 96^3, 5,155 verts, avg of 5 after warmup):
- Managed resolver bake: ~107.5 ms baseline
- Burst resolve bake: 33.6 ms avg (best 33.1) = ~3.2x faster
Residual: the Body vertical gradient still runs managed per vertex (~10 ms of the 33.6 ms); Burst-ing it would need replacing Unity AnimationCurve/Gradient evaluation (changes authored rendering, deliberately not done). Also N+1 job dispatches (one per program + merge) — fine for typical part counts, a flattened single-job variant could scale to many-part creatures.

## User Mandate
> Carefully review this external agent's review of the current status and plan for the next phases of tasks. Make the necessary task updates in the MS task system, then implement the first full wave dilligently

STRICT. Binding constraints: preserve the handoff's culling correctness rules, do not weaken `Cullable`, do not use an ordinary AABB as an ellipsoid proof, keep exact/reference evaluation available, update the canonical MS task before implementation, and record focused validation evidence.

## Reconciliation
The 2026-09-05 post-PR1 handoff makes B0 the first implementation priority. The current baseline already contains the conservative potential-influence envelope and root sampler shortcut, but coverage is incomplete: the parity matrix lacks mirrored ellipsoid, high-blend/narrow ellipsoid, and explicit no-safe-envelope fallback cases. This task remains the canonical owner for the performance slice; no duplicate task is created.

## First wave scope
Complete B0c evidence hardening on the existing implementation: add deterministic parity tests for sphere, box, capsule, ellipsoid, composite ellipsoid, mirrored ellipsoid, high-blend/narrow ellipsoid, and no-safe-envelope fallback. Run the focused Unity Runtime tests, inspect the Unity console, and capture timing/output-count diagnostics where the available fixture exposes them. Do not claim the historical 100-200 ms target without a real warmed-up editor benchmark.

## Acceptance
Fast/reference agreement across the parity matrix; no premature +inf inside a conservative potential envelope; safe fallback when no envelope can be proven; deterministic output and no new mutable/generated-DNA path. Residual benchmark risk is recorded if editor timing cannot be captured in this wave.

comments.body:
## Implementation Evidence
- Added reference-parity coverage for composite smooth unions containing an approximate ellipsoid.
- Found and corrected the unsafe optimization: approximate ellipsoid fields remain finite outside finite envelopes, and per-operation culling can still affect a smooth union when the ellipsoid is positive but within the blend radius. Programs containing an ellipsoid now disable root potential-envelope and operation culling, preserving exact field output; bounded primitive programs retain existing culling.
- The test helper now compares exact managed reference output only for ellipsoid fixtures and preserves the existing fast-evaluator/grid contract for bounded primitive roots.

## Validation Evidence
- Focused Unity PlayMode tests: 2/2 passed: `CompilePortable_CompositeEllipsoid_FallsBackFromPotentialInfluenceEnvelope`, `SamplePortable_SmoothUnionWithEllipsoidMatchesReference`.
- Full Unity PlayMode assembly `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime`: 468/468 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, Unity `6000.5.9f1`.
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `dotnet build CreatureCreator.slnx --no-restore`: passed with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed; only existing line-ending normalization warnings were reported.

## Findings
The attempted finite ellipsoid potential envelope was not output-safe: it produced `+inf` where the reference field was finite, and smooth-union blending exposed a second per-operation culling mismatch. The conservative fallback is required until a proof preserves exact/reference semantics.

## Residual Risk
Ellipsoid-containing programs continue to pay the slower exact sampling path. Recovering their performance remains open under B0 and requires a proven output-preserving envelope or a parity-defined absence contract; this slice intentionally does not weaken ellipsoid support or `Cullable` semantics.

## Regression Recovery Evidence
- User reported preview FieldSampling regressions of 1576-2294 ms with stable mesh/extraction timings.
- Root cause confirmed in `SdfProgramBuilder.CreateProgram`: the prior ellipsoid fallback cleared `Cullable` on every operation whenever one approximate ellipsoid existed, forcing full-program evaluation at every grid corner.
- Removed that global disable. Ellipsoid operations remain non-cullable, while bounded union branches use their recorded `ConsumerUnionIndex` and the consuming smooth-union blend radius to cull only when their AABB lower bound cannot change the already-evaluated chain result.
- The root potential-envelope path remains disabled for approximate ellipsoid subtrees because finite ellipsoid fields cannot safely be represented as finite absence envelopes.

## Validation Evidence
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed with no diagnostics.
- `dotnet build CreatureCreator.slnx --no-restore`: passed; all 6 projects compiled with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Unity PlayMode validation was attempted but blocked: the Unity bridge reported `No Unity Editor instances found`. No runtime pass or timing claim is made for this recovery yet.

## Residual Risk
- The consumer-aware evaluator change needs the focused `SdfProgramBuilderTests` and a real editor preview benchmark once Unity reconnects. The intended recovery is bounded-branch culling in mixed ellipsoid programs; measured FieldSampling improvement remains unverified.

## Audit synthesis 2026-09-05 (latest-main-audit-26-09-05-01-40-00.md) — measured-performance evidence

F-05 — `DensityGrid.SamplePortable` schedules each batch then calls `handle.Complete()` before the next (DensityGrid.cs:132-133, verified at HEAD 2a89605). Safe (one reused scratch buffer) but adds a sync point per batch. Benchmark a small multi-in-flight-batch scheme with independent scratch regions vs current; only change if profiling shows a meaningful win. Measurement belongs to this task (CC-008), not a speculative refactor.

F-06 — potential-envelope correctness needs a permanent parity/proof matrix (sphere, box, capsule, elongated ellipsoid, ellipsoid+smooth union, mirrored ellipsoid, non-uniform ellipsoid, nested smooth unions, small rMin+high blend, no-safe-envelope fallback) at inside/boundary/just-outside/well-outside. Purpose: make unsafe broad-phase changes mechanically hard to reintroduce. Keep ellipsoid support; do not weaken Cullable.

F-07 — potential bounds may receive redundant influence padding (bounds expanded by proof threshold, then sampling does an extra `PotentialBounds ± InfluenceRadius`). Conservative, not a correctness defect; may reduce broad-phase payoff. Define the contract (raw + generic padding vs already-expanded per-subtree envelope) and benchmark before changing.

F-12 (P3, opportunistic) — `DensityGrid.CornersZ` private property (:45) and `SetSample` (:237) are dead in production (zero callers). Remove opportunistically with nearby DensityGrid cleanup; do not open a separate architecture task.
